chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

OpenHands is an **AI-driven software engineering agent ecosystem**, not a single binary. Official materials (2026) separate concerns:

| Surface | Repo / package | Role (DOCUMENTED) |
|---------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Software Agent SDK** | `OpenHands/software-agent-sdk` — packages `openhands.sdk`, `openhands.tools`, `openhands.workspace`, `openhands.agent_server` | Canonical agent loop, tools, workspaces, events, security, Agent Server HTTP/WS |
| **Agent Canvas** | `OpenHands/OpenHands` (README: “self-hosted developer control center”) | UI / control plane; can drive OpenHands agent **or** ACP-compatible third-party agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, …) |
| **Automation** | `OpenHands/automation` (referenced by SDK README) | Scheduling, webhooks, run history, dispatch (not deeply audited here) |
| **Legacy V0 app architecture** | Still documented under “architecture/runtime|backend” | CodeActAgent + EventStream + Docker/Local/Remote **Runtime** + Action Execution Server inside sandbox |

**DOCUMENTED (docs index):** V1 prefers the term **sandbox** over legacy **runtime**; some env knobs still named `RUNTIME` during migration.

**Identity claim (DOCUMENTED SDK overview):** SDK is source of truth for agent behavior; applications (Canvas, CLI, custom) consume SDK / Agent Server APIs.

Core coding-agent loop (V1 SDK, DOCUMENTED + OBSERVED examples):

- `Conversation` owns lifecycle/state/events
- Stateless `Agent.step()`: optional condense → LLM → parse tool calls → security/confirmation → execute tools → observations → loop
- Tools: typed Action / Observation / Executor (Terminal, FileEditor, TaskTracker, BrowserToolSet, MCP, planning/delegation presets, …)
- Workspace swap selects Local vs Remote execution without rewriting agent code

Legacy coding agent (DOCUMENTED `usage/agents`): **CodeActAgent** — unified code action space (bash + IPython via plugins); Converse vs CodeAct each turn.

chunks.title: V1 SDK local path (DOCUMENTED sequence)
chunks.content:
### V1 SDK local path (DOCUMENTED sequence)

```text
Input: user message → Conversation.send_message / run
  → Agent.step():
       pending confirmed actions? → execute → ObservationEvents → return
       condenser? → View | Condensation event
       LLM(history + tools + skills)
       context overflow? → CondensationRequest
       tool calls? → ActionEvents
         → confirmation policy? → WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION
         → else SecurityAnalyzer risk → execute ToolExecutor in workspace
       → ObservationEvents → loop
       message only? → MessageEvent → user
  → StuckDetector may flag repetitive patterns (default on)
  → optional Critic on FinishAction → iterative refinement
Final Output: conversation events + workspace side effects (files/commands/browser)
```

chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

**DOCUMENTED** — Pydantic AI is an open-source **Python agent SDK** from the Pydantic team: a typed agent loop (`Agent`), model-agnostic providers, function tools / toolsets / MCP / native tools, structured `output_type` validated by Pydantic, dependency injection via `deps_type` + `RunContext`, optional graph orchestration (`pydantic-graph`), OpenTelemetry instrumentation (first-party Logfire), durable execution adapters (Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, Restate, AWS Lambda durable; plus external Kitaru/Airflow), and a separate **Harness** package (`pydantic-ai-harness`) for coding-agent capabilities.

Canonical positioning (README + docs): “typed end to end”, FastAPI-like DX, same agent runnable behind CLI / web / realtime voice / durable queue.

**Not claimed here as measured:** production reliability vs peers; token efficiency; “best framework”. Stars (~20k) are adoption signal only — separated in §5.

chunks.title: 2. Architecture map
chunks.content:
## 2. Architecture map

```text
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Agent[DepsT, OutputT]                  │
                    │  instructions · tools/toolsets          │
                    │  output_type · deps_type · capabilities │
                    │  model settings · retries               │
                    └──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                                       │
              run / run_sync / stream / iter / realtime
                                       │
                                       ▼
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  pydantic-graph agent run (internal)               │
         │  UserPromptNode → ModelRequestNode → CallToolsNode │
         │  … (retry / validation loops) → End[FinalResult]   │
         └───────────────┬────────────────────┬───────────────┘
                         │                    │
                         ▼                    ▼
              ┌──────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────────┐
              │ Model + Provider │   │ Toolsets / Capabilities│
              │ + ModelProfile   │   │ MCP · native · deferred│
              └──────────────────┘   └────────────────────────┘
                         │                    │
                         ▼                    ▼
              ┌──────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────────┐
              │ Structured output│   │ RunContext[DepsT]      │
              │ validators /     │   │ deps · usage · retry   │
              │ ModelRetry       │   │ enqueue · emit         │
              └──────────────────┘   └────────────────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
              AgentRunResult[OutputT] (+ messages, usage)
                         │
         optional: OTel/Logfire · DurableExec · Evals · Harness
```

**DOCUMENTED** components of an Agent: instructions, function tools/toolsets, structured output type, dependency type constraint, LLM model, model settings, capabilities (reusable bundles of tools/hooks/instructions/settings).

**Separate product surface (stack):** Pydantic Validation · Pydantic AI · Logfire · AI Gateway · Pydantic Evals · Pydantic Graph · genai-prices · Harness.

chunks.title: 3. Execution flow
chunks.content:
## 3. Execution flow

```text
Input (user prompt + deps + optional message_history / usage_limits)
  → build agent graph (prompts, tools, output schemas)
  → UserPromptNode / instruction assembly (incl. dynamic system prompts via RunContext)
  → ModelRequestNode (Model + Provider + Profile; optional before_model_request hooks)
  → ModelResponse (text / tool calls / output-tool calls)
  → CallToolsNode: validate tool args (Pydantic) → execute tools → ToolReturn parts
       OR validate structured output / output function → optional output_validator
       OR ModelRetry / validation failure → RetryPromptPart (tool vs output budgets)
  → loop until End(FinalResult[OutputT]) or UnexpectedModelBehavior / usage limit
  → Final Output: AgentRunResult.output (typed) + all_messages + RunUsage
```

**DOCUMENTED** via Agents “Running Agents” + `Agent.iter` node list (UserPromptNode → ModelRequestNode → CallToolsNode → End). Streaming variants (`run_stream`, `run_stream_events`) change when the run is considered finished (`end_strategy` matters for dangling tool calls).

chunks.title: 4. Mechanisms (lens-aligned)
chunks.content:
## 4. Mechanisms (lens-aligned)

| id | problem | mechanism | evidence label | utility |
|----|---------|-----------|----------------|---------|
| PAI-AGENT | Need a reusable LLM “conversation unit” with typed I/O | `Agent[DepsT, OutputT]` as FastAPI-like app object; run/stream/iter/realtime | DOCUMENTED | HIGH for Python apps |
| PAI-DEPS | Inject DB/HTTP/user context into prompts/tools/validators without globals | `deps_type` + `RunContext[Deps].deps`; `override()` for tests | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-TOOLS | Let model call typed side effects / retrieval | `@tool` / `@tool_plain` / `Tool` / toolsets; schema from signature+docstring (griffe); args validated before call | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-OUTPUT | Force validated final value | `output_type` (models, unions, output functions); default tool-output mode; Native/Prompted markers | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-VALIDATE | Recover from bad model I/O | Pydantic validation + `ModelRetry` + separate tool/output retry budgets + `output_validator` | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-MODEL | Swap vendors without rewriting agent | `provider:model` string or Model/Provider/Profile; FallbackModel; ConcurrencyLimitedModel; TestModel/FunctionModel | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-TOOL-EXEC | Execute/orchestrate tool results in the loop | CallToolsNode; combined toolset; MCP; native tools; deferred/HITL tools; max_concurrency / tool_timeout | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-GRAPH | Explicit FSM/workflows beyond agent loop | `pydantic-graph` (standalone); agent loop itself is a graph; `Agent.iter`/`next` for control | DOCUMENTED | MED–HIGH (advanced) |
| PAI-CONTEXT | Runtime context + history + progressive capability load | RunContext fields; message_history; Capability `defer_loading`; enqueue/emit mid-run | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-DURABLE | Survive restarts / long runs / HITL | TemporalDurability / DBOS / Prefect / Restate / Lambda (+ Kitaru/Airflow); activities for model/tool | DOCUMENTED | HIGH when ops need it |
| PAI-OTEL | Observe model+tool spans/cost | `logfire.instrument_pydantic_ai()`; OTel-native; genai-prices | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-TYPES | Catch wiring errors at write-time | Generics + Pydantic schemas; IDE/type-checker alignment on tools/output | DOCUMENTED | HIGH (Python) |
| PAI-CAPABILITY | Package reusable agent behavior | `Capability` / `capabilities=[…]` (tools+instructions+hooks); Harness compositions | DOCUMENTED | HIGH |
| PAI-EVALS | Measure agent behavior | Pydantic Evals (OSS; Logfire UI optional) | DOCUMENTED | MED (product-adjacent) |

chunks.title: Attack 1 — “Just copy Modes into MegaBrain”
chunks.content:
## Attack 1 — “Just copy Modes into MegaBrain”

**Temptation:** Roo’s mode system is famous and clear → implement `kind: Mode` registry.

**Rebuttal:** MegaBrain already has PDA roles, skills, Capability/Provider registries, Policy. A parallel Mode registry is duplication (`REJECT` second registry). Correct move is `ADAPT`: encode specialization as skill/capability ACL packages, not port Roo YAML.

**Verdict:** Held — decisions use ADAPT/ALREADY_PRESENT/REJECT appropriately.

chunks.title: Attack 2 — “Orchestrator with empty tools is clearly superior”
chunks.content:
## Attack 2 — “Orchestrator with empty tools is clearly superior”

**Temptation:** Treat Boomerang as best-practice mandate.

**Rebuttal:** Evidence is `DOCUMENTED` design rationale (context poisoning), not measured win rates. MegaBrain already has an orchestrator role class. Summary-only handoffs may **lose** evidence fidelity vs Evidence Bus — trade-off, not free lunch. Nested subtasks have documented UX failure modes.

**Verdict:** Held — ADAPT handoff contract; not ADOPT wholesale.

chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

Roo Code was an **open-source (Apache-2.0) VS Code extension** that presents a chat agent with **modes** (personas + tool-group permissions), **HITL approval** (with optional auto-approve), **MCP** client support, **project/global rules**, **context mentions**, optional **semantic codebase indexing**, and **Orchestrator / Boomerang subtasks** for multi-mode delegation.

**Product state as of research date:** extension suite shut down; repo archived; docs site still describes the architecture as it existed at sunset. Successor product marketing (Roomote / roocode.com pivot) is **out of mechanism scope** unless needed for lifecycle — not mined as architecture.

**Identity signals (`OBSERVED` / `DOCUMENTED`):**

- Repo: `RooCodeInc/Roo-Code` — description “whole dev team of AI agents in your code editor”
- Stars ~24.3k, forks ~3.4k (`OBSERVED` API)
- License Apache-2.0 (`OBSERVED`)
- Docs: https://docs.roocode.com/ (+ GitHub Pages mirror referenced in README)

---

chunks.title: 2. Architecture map
chunks.content:
## 2. Architecture map

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  VS Code Extension Host (Roo Code)                               │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Chat UI     │  │ Mode selector│  │ Auto-approve / settings │ │
│  │ @mentions   │  │ Sticky model │  │ MCP Servers view        │ │
│  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └───────────┬─────────────┘ │
│         │                │                      │               │
│         ▼                ▼                      ▼               │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ Prompt assembly: roleDefinition + customInstructions +   │   │
│  │ rules (~/.roo, .roo/, .roorules*, AGENTS.md) + tool guide│   │
│  └───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘   │
│                              ▼                                  │
│  ┌──────────────┐     LLM Provider (BYOK / local)               │
│  │ Task runtime │◄─── Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter/Ollama/…     │
│  │ (parent/sub) │                                               │
│  └──────┬───────┘                                               │
│         │ tool calls gated by mode.groups + approvals           │
│         ▼                                                       │
│  Tool groups: read | edit | command | mcp | modes               │
│  (+ new_task / switch_mode / attempt_completion / …)            │
│         │                                                       │
│         ├── FS / terminal / browser(deprecated group)           │
│         ├── MCP hub (use_mcp_tool, access_mcp_resource)         │
│         └── Optional Qdrant + embedder → codebase_search        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Specialization model:** Modes = **Agent specialization packages** (role prompt + optional `whenToUse` + tool group ACL + sticky model). Not a separate multi-process agent fleet by default — one chat agent whose **capability surface** changes with mode; Orchestrator adds **hierarchical tasks**.

chunks.title: 3. Execution flow (documented)
chunks.content:
## 3. Execution flow (documented)

```text
User message (+ optional @mentions / slash)
  → Mode selected (dropdown | /mode | sticky persistence | switch_mode)
  → System prompt = roleDefinition + instructions + layered Rules
  → LLM proposes tool use
  → Permission check: mode.groups ∩ tool ∈ group
  → HITL approve | auto-approve (per permission tiles) | .rooignore block
  → Tool result → conversation
  → [Orchestrator path] new_task(mode, message[, todos])
        → parent pauses; child task isolated context
        → child attempt_completion(result summary)
        → parent resumes with summary only
  → attempt_completion / user stop → Final Output (edits, answers, plan)
```

Labels: flow shape `DOCUMENTED` (using-modes, boomerang-tasks, new_task, auto-approving, custom-instructions). Exact internal scheduler / prompt token packing: `UNKNOWN` (not fully reverse-traced in this pass).

chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

SWE-agent is an open-source **LM software-engineering agent** that takes a problem statement (typically a GitHub issue / SWE-bench instance) and iteratively uses tools inside a **sandboxed shell** to browse, edit, run code, and emit a **git patch**. Core research claim: performance depends heavily on an **Agent-Computer Interface (ACI)** — LM-centric commands and feedback formats — not only on the base model (`DOCUMENTED` paper + docs).

**Product / lifecycle status (`DOCUMENTED`):** Official site and README recommend **mini-swe-agent** as successor; SWE-agent itself is **maintenance-only**. mini-swe-agent drops custom tools for bash-only + independent subprocess execution; SWE-agent remains the configurable ACI / history-processor / tool-bundle research scaffold.

**Related ecosystem (`DOCUMENTED`, not fully reverse-engineered here):** SWE-ReX (runtime), SWE-bench / sb-cli (eval), SWE-smith / SWE-agent-LM (open-weights models), EnIGMA mode (CTF; pinned to v0.7 for full features).

---

chunks.title: 2. Architecture map
chunks.content:
## 2. Architecture map

```text
CLI `sweagent` (run | run-batch)
        │
        ├─► SWEEnv ──thin wrapper──► SWE-ReX Deployment
        │         (Docker local | Modal | AWS | …)
        │              └─► container + stateful bash session
        │              └─► install tool bundles (ACI) into PATH
        │
        └─► Agent (yaml-configured)
                 ├─ templates (system / instance / next_step / demos)
                 ├─ ToolHandler (bundles + bash + parsers + blocklist)
                 ├─ HistoryProcessor(s)
                 ├─ Model (litellm; cost/call limits)
                 └─ optional RetryAgent / Reviewer loops
```

Sources: `docs/background/architecture.md`, `sweagent/environment/swe_env.py`, `sweagent/agent/agents.py`, `pyproject.toml` (`swe-rex>=1.4.0`, `litellm`) — labels `DOCUMENTED` + `OBSERVED`.

**Default tool surface (1.x `config/default.yaml`, `OBSERVED`):** bash enabled; bundles `tools/registry`, `tools/edit_anthropic` (str_replace editor + filemap), `tools/review_on_submit_m`; parse via `function_calling`; history `cache_control` last_n=2. Classical paper ACI (`windowed` viewer, `search_*`, linting `edit`) still ships as alternate bundles under `tools/` (`OBSERVED` tree).

---

chunks.title: 3. Execution flow
chunks.content:
## 3. Execution flow

```text
Input: problem_statement + repo + deployment image/config
  → SWEEnv.start: deploy runtime, create bash session, copy/reset repo
  → Agent.setup: install tools, load templates/demos, init history
  → LOOP:
       HistoryProcessors(history) → model.query
       → parse thought+action (function_calling | thought_action | …)
       → blocklist / bash -n checks → requery up to max_requeries
       → execute in shell session (SWE-ReX) → observation (+ state JSON)
       → append history + trajectory step
       → until submit token / done / cost|context|timeout|format exit
  → On many exits: autosubmit `git add -A && git diff --cached > /root/model.patch`
  → Output: trajectory (*.traj), model.patch / preds.json (batch), optional local apply / PR
```

Labels: loop/autosubmit `OBSERVED` in `agents.py`; env communicate `OBSERVED` in `swe_env.py`; batch preds `DOCUMENTED` batch_mode docs.

**Planning:** Not a separate planner graph. Planning is **in-prompt** (instance template steps: localize → reproduce → edit → re-run → edge cases) + free-form LM thought each turn (`DOCUMENTED`/`OBSERVED` default.yaml). Optional `RetryAgent` + reviewer/chooser for multi-attempt selection (`OBSERVED` `reviewer.py` symbols).

**Validation:** (1) edit-time lint reject (paper ACI / flake8 helper) (`DOCUMENTED`/`OBSERVED`); (2) agent-authored reproduce scripts + tests in env (`DOCUMENTED` prompt); (3) SWE-bench harness via sb-cli / `--evaluate` (`DOCUMENTED`); (4) submit-time review messages asking revert of test edits (`OBSERVED` default.yaml). **No** MegaBrain-style Evidence Bus gates.

chunks.title: 1. Strongest claim under fire
chunks.content:
## 1. Strongest claim under fire

**Claim:** This corpus is a **persona roster + distribution adapters + coordination docs**, not an executable multi-agent runtime.

**Attack:** NEXUS + Agents Orchestrator + Hermes `delegate` + host “subagents” could constitute a real multi-agent system in practice.

**Defense:**
- `SECURITY.md` explicitly classifies agent files as non-executable prompt definitions and the repo as definitions + install/convert scripts (`DOCUMENTED`).
- No in-tree scheduler, message bus, agent process manager, or `package.json`/app runtime (`OBSERVED`).
- `agents-orchestrator` itself is a Markdown persona whose “spawn” steps are natural-language instructions to the host (`OBSERVED`).
- Hermes router is an **adapter** whose generated artifact is gitignored; even then it composes prompts/tools for Hermes — host still owns execution (`DOCUMENTED` / `OBSERVED` absence).

**Residual risk:** Hosts may implement true subagent runtimes. That would be **host architecture**, not Agency’s. Marked `U-AA-06`. Claim stands for **this LOCAL_CORPUS**.

**Verdict:** Claim **holds** for target as defined.

chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

**OBSERVED:** A public MIT repository whose *primary deliverable* is a **roster of specialist agent personas** as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, organized into **18 divisions** (`divisions.json`), plus:

- Shell/Python **distribution tooling** (`scripts/install.sh`, `convert.sh`, lint/check/test-* for install/convert integrity)
- A **tool install contract catalog** (`tools.json`) describing how to render/install into host coding agents
- **NEXUS** strategy docs: playbooks, runbooks, handoff templates, activation prompts (coordination *doctrine*, not a runtime)
- Thin `integrations/*/README.md` stubs; generated per-tool trees are **intentionally not committed**
- Optional MCP-memory *pattern docs* (prompt add-ons + example)

**DOCUMENTED (SECURITY.md):** *“This repository contains Markdown-based agent definitions and shell scripts for installation and conversion.”* Agent `.md` files are *“Non-executable prompt definitions.”*

**DOCUMENTED (README):** Host activation is copy/install into Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / etc., then natural-language activation (“activate Frontend Developer mode…”). A separate native app (`agency-agents-app`) browses/installs the roster — **code absent from this corpus**.

chunks.title: Critical classification: roster ≠ multi-agent runtime
chunks.content:
### Critical classification: roster ≠ multi-agent runtime

| Layer | What it is | Evidence |
|-------|------------|----------|
| Roster / catalog | 279 persona `.md` with `name:` frontmatter under division dirs | `OBSERVED` file inventory; Hermes README cites “Generated agent count: 279” |
| Prompt architecture | Identity, mission, rules, deliverables, workflow, metrics sections | `OBSERVED` + `CONTRIBUTING` template |
| Coordination doctrine | NEXUS phases, handoff markdown templates, “spawn X agent” prompt text | `DOCUMENTED` in `strategy/` |
| Distribution | convert → install into host tool formats (`per-agent` / `roster` / `plugin`) | `OBSERVED` `tools.json`, scripts (unread as executed) |
| Host runtime | Whatever Claude Code / Cursor / Hermes / … provides | **Outside this repo** |
| Executable multi-agent system | Shared state machine, scheduler, message bus, agent processes | **ABSENT** in corpus (`package.json`/app runtime absent; SECURITY confirms non-executable agents) |

**INFERRED (premises: SECURITY.md + absence of orchestrator code + orchestrator being itself a persona):** “Multi-agent” behaviour, when it happens, is **host LLM following instructions** to switch persona / ask for subagents — not a first-party agency runtime shipping here.

chunks.title: What could be wrong in this investigation?
chunks.content:
## What could be wrong in this investigation?

1. **Over-weighting packaging novelty.** Multi-path symlinks and marketplace JSON are clear OBSERVED patterns, but may be table-stakes for public Agent Skills — not unique “architecture”. Decisions should stay packaging/DX scoped; they are.

2. **Inferring Pages-mirror intent.** EXACT_DUPLICATE is proven; “why” remains UNKNOWN. Report marks INFERRED only — good. Do not promote U-BR-02 to fact.

3. **Scope creep into Hyperframes.** SKILL.md names sibling skills and `npx hyperframes check`. We did not open that stack. Any claim about render quality, contrast lint, or beat sync is DOCUMENTED instruction text, not MEASURED behavior.

4. **Demo ≠ eval.** README “benchmark suite” language is easy to launder into evaluation claims. Explicitly REJECTED as eval substitute.

5. **Baseline comparison thin by design.** MegaBrain has no video skill; EQUIVALENCE ratings are analogy (Capability/Provider, skill refs). That is honest PARTIAL/SUBSTANTIAL, but easy to overclaim ALREADY_PRESENT — reserved mainly for progressive-disclosure + tool ownership split.

chunks.title: 1. What exists?
chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

`brag` is a **single Agent Skill** (`/brag`) that instructs an agent to turn the current project’s website/app into a short launch video via **Hyperframes** (external CLI + sibling Hyperframes skills). The repository is intentionally a **distribution + demonstration vehicle**, not an agent runtime.

**OBSERVED inventory (high level):**

| Area | Contents |
|------|----------|
| Canonical skill | `skills/brag/` — `SKILL.md`, `references/` (inspect→plan→compose→deliver + tones + audio), bundled `assets/` (music/SFX + cue metadata), maintainer `scripts/` |
| Multi-agent discovery | Symlinks (git mode `120000`): `.claude/skills/brag`, `.agents/skills/brag`, `.opencode/skills/brag` → `../../skills/brag` |
| Claude plugin packaging | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `marketplace.json` |
| Examples / “benchmark suite” | `examples/` — 5 fake product sites + committed `brag.mp4` |
| Launch docs site | `docs/` — static HTML/CSS/JS, GitHub Pages root; gallery uses `docs/examples/{horse-tinder,fish-flight-school,taxi-for-taxis}/` |
| DX check | `scripts/check-docs.mjs` — local href/src existence + gallery count copy consistency |
| Product copy | Root `PRODUCT.md` + per-example `PRODUCT.md` |

**Size / media dominance (corpus audit, OBSERVED):** ~74.8 MiB / ~340 files; dominated by audio/video. Sample durations (MEASURED by prior audit ffprobe): example videos ~21–23s; music beds ~1–3 min; UI SFX ~tens of ms.

**EXACT_DUPLICATE (OBSERVED, corpus `DUPLICATE-REPORT.md` + reconfirmed md5 on `index.html`):** for three gallery examples, `docs/examples/<slug>/{brag.mp4,index.html,styles.css}` ≡ `examples/<slug>/` byte-for-byte. Docs trees additionally carry `brag.jpg` + `site.jpg` (not mirrored in `examples/`). Two more examples (`bicycles-for-snakes`, `psychologists-for-chatbots`) live only under `examples/`. One SFX pair is byte-identical under different filenames (`footstep_carpet_003/004.ogg`).

**Not present (OBSERVED):** automated evals/tests for the skill; Hyperframes implementation; agent transcripts; CHANGELOG.

chunks.content:
## 1. What exists?

A **curated library of Agent Skills** for engineering and productivity workflows, packaged as:

- **38** `SKILL.md` packages under bucket folders (`engineering/`, `productivity/`, `misc/`, `in-progress/`; `deprecated/` exists as lifecycle sink).
- **25** promoted skills listed in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (exact curated ship set).
- Dual-harness metadata: Claude frontmatter + per-skill `agents/openai.yaml` (Codex UI + implicit-invocation policy).
- Contributor contracts in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (symlink pair — OBSERVED via docs; symlink claim DOCUMENTED in CHANGELOG 1.2.0).
- Human docs mirror at `docs/<bucket>/<skill>.md` (25 pages) with publish template.
- Repo-level ADRs under `.agents/adr/` (distribution + setup-dependency policy).
- Domain self-model: root `CONTEXT.md` + skill `domain-modeling` formats.
- Release tooling: Changesets, `CHANGELOG.md`, `scripts/sync-plugin-version.mjs` (not executed here).
- Dev symlink installer `scripts/link-skills.sh` (maintainer-only; not end-user path).

**Not present (OBSERVED):** automated tests, eval harness, runtime orchestrator, tool registry, MCP servers as first-class artifacts.

**Identity note (OBSERVED):** folder name `skills` ≠ npm/plugin name `mattpocock-skills`.

chunks.title: 2. Architecture map
chunks.content:
## 2. Architecture map

```text
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Distribution                       │
                    │  • Claude plugin (curated paths)    │
                    │  • skills.sh / npx skills add       │
                    │  • link-skills.sh (maintainer)      │
                    └─────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                      │
┌─────────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Bucket lifecycle                                                          │
│  promoted: engineering/ + productivity/  → README + plugin.json + docs/    │
│  beta: in-progress/   kept: misc/   sink: deprecated/                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                      │
          ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
          ▼                           ▼                           ▼
   User-invoked                 Model-invoked              Shared reference
   disable-model-               description triggers       (model-invoked so
   invocation: true             + Skill-tool callable      others can Call)
   + openai policy false
          │                           │
          │    Call Skill tool        │
          └──────────►────────────────┘
                                      │
                                      ▼
                         Per-repo config (setup skill)
                         CLAUDE/AGENTS ## Agent skills
                         docs/agents/{issue-tracker,domain,triage-labels}.md
                         CONTEXT.md + docs/adr/
```

**Composition graph (DOCUMENTED in `ask-matt` + OBSERVED wrappers):**

```text
Main flow:  grill-with-docs → (optional prototype/handoff) → to-spec → to-tickets → implement
                                                              implement → tdd + code-review
Wrappers:   grill-me → grilling
            grill-with-docs → grilling + domain-modeling
Router:     ask-matt (human index over user-invoked skills; does not Skill-tool them)
Primitives: grilling, domain-modeling, codebase-design, writing-for-agents, tdd, …
```

chunks.title: 3. Execution flow (or UNKNOWN)
chunks.content:
## 3. Execution flow (or UNKNOWN)

Harness runtime behaviour is **UNKNOWN** (not executed). Documented intended flow:

```text
Human installs (plugin | skills.sh)
  → optional /setup-matt-pocock-skills (writes AGENTS/CLAUDE pointers + docs/agents/*)
  → Human types /skill  OR  model matches description (model-invoked only)
  → Agent loads SKILL.md body
  → If wrapper: Call Skill tool → load primitive(s)
  → Steps with completion criteria; optional subagents / tracker I/O
  → Artifacts: CONTEXT.md, ADRs, issues/tickets, code, handoff md, HTML reports, …
```

Epistemic: flow shape is **DOCUMENTED**; actual tool binding, discovery ranking, and failure recovery inside Claude Code / Codex = **UNKNOWN**.

chunks.title: 4. Mechanisms
chunks.content:
## 4. Mechanisms

| id | problem | mechanism | evidence label | utility |
|----|---------|-----------|----------------|---------|
| M-BUCKETS | Ship only stable skills; keep drafts visible | Bucket folders + plugin explicit path list | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-INVOKE-AXIS | Orchestrators must not auto-fire; primitives must | User- vs model-invoked + dual harness flags | OBSERVED + DOCUMENTED | USEFUL |
| M-SKILL-TOOL-COMPOSE | Reuse discipline without duplicating bodies | Explicit `Call the Skill tool with "name"` | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-THIN-WRAPPER | User entrypoints without context load of primitives | 1-line wrappers (`grill-me`, `grill-with-docs`) | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-ROUTER | Cognitive load of many user-invoked skills | `ask-matt` human router map | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-WRITE-AGENTS | Brittle/verbose agent docs | `writing-for-agents`: pointers, hierarchy, leading words, criteria | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-SETUP-HARD-SOFT | Config needed unevenly | Setup skill + ADR hard vs soft dependency pointers | DOCUMENTED + OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-CONTEXT-ADR | Misalignment + verbose jargon | `CONTEXT.md` glossary + minimal ADRs | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-MAIN-FLOW | Idea→ship across sessions | Spec/tickets/implement + phase boundaries | DOCUMENTED | CONDITIONALLY_USEFUL |
| M-DUAL-DISTRO | Subscribe vs fork | Claude plugin curated vs skills.sh editable | DOCUMENTED | USEFUL |
| M-HUMAN-DOCS | Humans forget when to invoke | `docs/` 4-section pages + writing-docs contract | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-RELEASE | Version drift plugin↔package | Changesets + sync-plugin-version | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-AXIS-ISOLATE | Mixed review criteria pollute | Parallel Standards/Spec subagents | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-GRILL-TREE | Premature build / silent assumptions | Design-tree frontier interview rounds | OBSERVED | USEFUL |
| M-HARNESS-NEUTRAL | Claude-specific wording breaks Codex | Drop harness tool names from prompts (1.2.3) | DOCUMENTED | USEFUL |

chunks.title: 1. Dual-harness metadata (1.2.0)
chunks.content:
### 1. Dual-harness metadata (1.2.0)

**Change:** Add `agents/openai.yaml` beside every skill; Codex `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` pairs with Claude `disable-model-invocation`; `AGENTS.md` symlink to `CLAUDE.md`.  
**Why (DOCUMENTED):** One set works in Claude Code and Codex without generated copies.  
**Implication for mining:** Invocation axis is a *deliberate product of evolution*, not an accident of one harness.

chunks.title: 2. Native Claude plugin + marketplace (1.2.0)
chunks.content:
### 2. Native Claude plugin + marketplace (1.2.0)

**Change:** `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` curated path list; later accepted into official marketplace; skills.sh remains universal path.  
**Why (ADR 0002):** Subscribe/read-only vs fork/edit; Codex plugin blocked by single-path + symlink drop.  
**Implication:** Bucket layout is load-bearing for distribution, not only taxonomy.

chunks.title: 3. Graduation pipeline (1.2.x)
chunks.content:
### 3. Graduation pipeline (1.2.x)

**Examples:** `to-questionnaire`, `wizard` move from `in-progress/` → promoted buckets with plugin entry, README, docs page, ask-matt route.  
**Implication:** `in-progress/` is a public beta channel with explicit non-ship invariant.

chunks.title: 4. Invocation polarity flips (1.2.2)
chunks.content:
### 4. Invocation polarity flips (1.2.2)

**Example:** `writing-for-agents` had Codex policy false → filtered from model-visible list → fixed by dropping policy and moving README category to Model-invoked.  
**Implication:** Dual flags drift is a real failure mode (supports M-INVOKE-AXIS costs).

chunks.title: 5. Harness neutralization (1.2.3)
chunks.content:
### 5. Harness neutralization (1.2.3)

**Change:** Remove Claude-specific tool/agent-type names from subagent instructions in several skills.  
**Implication:** Cross-harness portability is an ongoing edit discipline (M-HARNESS-NEUTRAL).

chunks.content:

**Change:** `diagnosing-bugs` redaction section; wizard drops time estimates.  
**Implication:** Skills that show secrets/commands accumulate guardrail text over time.

chunks.title: What could be overclaimed?
chunks.content:
### What could be overclaimed?

1. **Treating prompt procedures as runtime.** The sandbox and artifact-promotion sequences are detailed and sound on paper (DOCUMENTED). Without harness code, claiming they “work” would be false. Report marks implementation ABSENT / DEFER — **kept**.
2. **Equating schema unit tests with security efficacy.** Tests OBSERVED target validator semantics (fixtures, severity caps, hostile diagnostics). They do **not** prove the six-phase workflow finds real vulns. U-SA-06/C-SA-02 capture this.
3. **Inflating MegaBrain gaps.** PDA critic/gate and Evidence Bus already cover independence and structured evidence at a generic level. Several decisions are ADAPT of **shapes**, not ALREADY_PRESENT of **security product** — deliberate to avoid proposing a second registry.
4. **ADOPT temptation.** No ADOPT issued. High-quality external skill ≠ drop-in MegaBrain module.

chunks.title: What could be underclaimed?
chunks.content:
### What could be underclaimed?

1. **Validator code quality.** ~1.6k LOC of careful zero-dep validation (limits, NFC/encoding for coverage IDs, state invariants) is stronger than “docs with a schema.” Confidence HIGH on *existence and design intent*; MEDIUM on *runtime pass* because tests not run.
2. **AI-AND-LLM companion.** Explicitly separates prompt injection theater from deterministic authority/binding failures — high architectural signal for agent-security, not fully mined into Level 2 findings (depth MODERATE).

## 1. What exists?

**OBSERVED:** Public Cloudflare repository packaged as an Anthropic-style Agent Skill (`skills/security-audit/`). It is not a runtime framework: orchestration is **prompt + parent-agent procedure**; the only executable artifacts in-corpus are zero-dependency Node validators and their unit tests.

**DOCUMENTED (README):** Seed of Cloudflare’s vulnerability-discovery harness (“Build your own vulnerability harness”); the multi-stage fleet system grew from this skill and is **absent** from this corpus.

Core product surface:

| Layer | Contents |
|-------|----------|
| Skill contract | `SKILL.md` — modes, safety, profiles/budget, 6-phase overview, anti-patterns |
| Phase prompts | `RECONNAISSANCE.md`, `HUNTING.md`, `VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md` |
| Domain companions | 10 attack-class markdown packs (core + AI/LLM, web/auth, client, memory/binary, supply-chain, cloud, RPC, availability, data lifecycle, desktop/IPC) |
| Output contracts | `report-schema.json`; parent-owned `findings.json`, `coverage-ledger.json`, prose reports |
| Machine gates | `validate-findings.cjs`, `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` (+ `.test.cjs`) |

chunks.title: 2. Architecture map
chunks.content:
## 2. Architecture map

```text
User request
    │
    ├─ guidance mode ──► selective methodology (no full artifacts)
    │
    └─ full audit mode
           │
           ▼
     Parent (sole writer of shared state)
           │
           ├─ run-metadata.json  (profile, budget, source_ref, status)
           ├─ architecture.md    (~1k word cap)
           ├─ coverage-ledger.json  ◄── validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
           └─ findings.json         ◄── validate-findings.cjs + report-schema.json
           │
     Phase 1  research×N  (map; no file writes)
     Phase 2  general hunters + research coverage critics (waves)
     Phase 3  fresh general verifiers (refute candidates)
     Phase 4  parent writes findings; both validators
     Phase 5  fresh research verifiers (record check; material replace → re-verify)
     Phase 6  derive REPORT.md / FINDINGS-DETAIL.md / NEEDS-VALIDATION.md
           │
     Terminal: complete (validators pass) | incomplete (explicit reason)
```

**Roles (agent-neutral terminology, OBSERVED in SKILL.md):** Parent · Task tool · `research` · `general`. Write isolation: agents write only `scratch/`; retained `artifacts/` via parent-side race-safe promotion procedure (DOCUMENTED in skill; **no harness implementation in corpus**).

```text
Input: explicit audit/pen-test request (+ optional output dir, profile, budget, scope)

  → Recon (parallel research) → architecture.md + seeded coverage ledger → ledger validator

  → findings.json + both validators
  → Phase 5 independent record verification (+ material replacement loop)
  → Phase 6 target-neutral prose derived from verified records only
Final Output: confirmed | needs_validation | rejected records + coverage claim + reports

```

## 1. What exists?

**OBSERVED:** Pacote MIT de **14 skills** (`skills/*/SKILL.md`) + **bootstrap runtime** multi-harness (hooks SessionStart, plugins OpenCode/Pi/Cursor/Claude/Codex/Hermes/Devin/Kimi/…), scripts auxiliares SDD, servidor opcional de brainstorm visual, e bateria grande de testes de infraestrutura em `tests/`.

chunks.title: 1. Executive Summary & Foundational Axioms
chunks.content:
## 1. Executive Summary & Foundational Axioms

The EvolveLoop V2.5 Multiagent Architecture is composed of **10 specialized agents** operating under a strict separation of concerns, epistemological gating, and rigorous execution contracts.

chunks.title: Core Axioms
chunks.content:
### Core Axioms
1. **Zero Direct Code Mutation by Non-Executors:** Neither the Orchestrator nor analytical/review specialists may directly author or modify code files. All modifications must be delegated to dedicated, contract-bound execution subagents.
2. **Single-Objective Planning:** The Planner operates strictly on a single atomic objective at any given phase to prevent scope drift, context poisoning, and combinatorial explosion.
3. **Epistemological Grounding:** The Codebase Archaeologist and all analytical agents must qualify every statement, metric, or finding according to the 5-tier epistemological taxonomy: `VERIFIED_IN_CODE`, `MEASURED`, `REPORTED_UNVERIFIED`, `INFERENCE`, or `DECISION_REQUIRED`.
4. **Independent Adversarial Review:** Work products cannot be certified by the agent that produced them. An Independent Reviewer must validate artifacts against the delegation contract before merge or advancement.
5. **No Secret Leaks or Unchecked Side Effects:** CLI operations run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which demands programmatic boundaries, strict workspace encapsulation, and human gates for high-risk operations.

---

chunks.title: 2. Specialized Agents Directory
chunks.content:
## 2. Specialized Agents Directory

```mermaid
graph TD
    User([Human Operator]) --> Orchestrator[1. Orchestrator]
    Orchestrator --> Planner[2. Planner]
    Orchestrator --> Archaeologist[3. Codebase Archaeologist]
    Orchestrator --> KnowledgeArch[4. Knowledge Architect]
    Orchestrator --> SecuritySpec[5. Security & Isolation Specialist]
    Orchestrator --> BenchmarkSpec[6. Benchmark & Evaluation Specialist]
    Orchestrator --> ImplCoord[7. Implementation Coordinator]
    Orchestrator --> TestEng[8. Test & Regression Engineer]
    Orchestrator --> IndepReviewer[9. Independent Reviewer]
    Orchestrator --> DocSpec[10. Documentation & Evidence Specialist]
    
    ImplCoord --> ExecSubagent[Dedicated Executor Subagent]
```

---

chunks.title: Agent 1: Orchestrator
chunks.content:
### Agent 1: Orchestrator
- **Identifier:** `orchestrator`
- **Role & Purpose:** Master supervisor of the V2.5 lifecycle. Maintains the global execution state, enforces gates, delegates tasks to specialists, monitors progress, and manages human checkpoints.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - High-level workflow orchestration and task dispatching.
  - Verification of prerequisites and acceptance criteria before moving phases.
  - Escalation of deadlocks, ambiguities, or security risks to the human operator.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN** from directly writing code, modifying workspace source files, editing tests, or crafting scripts.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from bypassing human approvals or auto-approving blocked gates.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from executing speculative actions without formal delegation artifacts.
- **Inputs:** User directives, project requirements, gate outputs, review verdicts.
- **Expected Outputs:** Delegation requests, cycle plans, session status summaries (`STATUS.md`), gate decisions.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `send_message`, `manage_task`, `schedule`, `run_command` (read-only queries: `git status`, `ls`, `cat`), `view_file`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 2: Planner
chunks.content:
### Agent 2: Planner
- **Identifier:** `planner`
- **Role & Purpose:** Decomposes incoming goals into deterministic Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), defines capability interfaces, evaluates critical paths, and synthesizes step-by-step implementation plans.
- **Core Invariant:** **Rule of One Objective** — Evaluates and plans exactly **one** primary objective per cycle. Multi-objective requests must be partitioned into sequential or independently gated milestones.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Task decomposition, dependency mapping, and interface contract generation.
  - Defining explicit DoD (Definition of Done) and Acceptance Criteria for each sub-task.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from modifying implementation code or test suites.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from planning multiple disjoint goals in a single cycle.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from omitting verification checkpoints or evidence criteria in tasks.
- **Inputs:** Feature brief, user requirements, current codebase topology from Archaeologist.
- **Expected Outputs:** Execution Plan artifacts (`PLAN.md`), Capability IR, DAG dependency matrices.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `write_file` (scoped strictly to `docs/v2.5/plans/` or `<artifactDir>`), `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 3: Codebase Archaeologist
chunks.content:
### Agent 3: Codebase Archaeologist
- **Identifier:** `codebase_archaeologist`
- **Role & Purpose:** Forensic explorer of the codebase. Investigates legacy implementations, traces dependencies, maps architectural layers, and surfaces ground truth without assumption.
- **Epistemological Taxonomy (Mandatory tagging for every claim):**
  1. `VERIFIED_IN_CODE`: Backed by literal line citations in source files.
  2. `MEASURED`: Empirically validated via profiling, command execution, or benchmark.
  3. `REPORTED_UNVERIFIED`: Documented in comments, commits, or legacy docs but not checked against current code.
  4. `INFERENCE`: Logical deduction or hypothesis derived from facts.
  5. `DECISION_REQUIRED`: Ambiguity, contradiction, or branch requiring architect/human resolution.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from mutating or refactoring code.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from presenting unverified assumptions as facts.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from guessing API behaviors without checking implementation or tests.
- **Inputs:** Research questions, file targets, architecture queries.
- **Expected Outputs:** Forensic dossiers (`RESEARCH_REPORT.md`), symbol references, dependency graphs.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `run_command` (strictly read-only: `grep`, `find`, `git log`, `ast-grep`, `rg`), `search_web`, `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 4: Knowledge Architect
chunks.content:
### Agent 4: Knowledge Architect
- **Identifier:** `knowledge_architect`
- **Role & Purpose:** Curates the persistent organizational memory, ADRs (Architectural Decision Records), domain models, and canonical project documentation.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Ingestion and synthesis of session findings into canonical knowledge structures.
  - Verification that new changes comply with established ADRs.
  - Managing the promotion queue from episodic memory (`.ai/sessions/`) to canonical wiki docs.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from blind writes to the canonical wiki without a validated promotion queue entry.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from editing application logic or runtime configuration.
- **Inputs:** Session logs, post-mortems, forensic dossiers, RFCs.
- **Expected Outputs:** Updated ADRs, canonical architecture docs (`docs/architecture/`), knowledge graphs.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `write_file` (scoped strictly to `docs/adr/`, `docs/architecture/`, `docs/concepts/`), `edit_file`, `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 5: Security & Isolation Specialist
chunks.content:
### Agent 5: Security & Isolation Specialist
- **Identifier:** `security_specialist`
- **Role & Purpose:** Enforces security guardrails, environment isolation, secrets hygiene, privilege boundaries, and policy validation.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Auditing commands and configurations for secret leaks, unsafe flags, or shell injections.
  - Ensuring worktrees and temporary branches do not break sandboxing rules.
  - Reviewing dependency trees for known CVEs and malicious manifests.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from disabling security gates or bypassing approval requirements.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from generating or storing plaintext credentials or test keys in source control.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from running arbitrary untrusted network binaries.
- **Inputs:** Delegation requests, script proposals, dependency manifests (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`).
- **Expected Outputs:** Security Audit Reports (`SECURITY_AUDIT.md`), Policy Compliance Matrices, Remediation Advisories.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `run_command` (security linters, audit tools: `npm audit`, `pip-audit`, `git diff`), `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 6: Benchmark & Evaluation Specialist
chunks.content:
### Agent 6: Benchmark & Evaluation Specialist
- **Identifier:** `eval_specialist`
- **Role & Purpose:** Designs, conducts, and interprets performance benchmarks, stress tests, latency measurements, and quantitative capability evaluations.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Profiling CPU, memory, I/O, and token usage.
  - Quantifying regressions against baseline metrics.
  - Producing reproducible benchmark scripts and statistical analyses.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from modifying production logic to "cheat" benchmarks.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from marking benchmarks as passed without persisting raw metric outputs (`MEASURED`).
- **Inputs:** Performance baselines, target latency/throughput SLA, test scripts.
- **Expected Outputs:** Benchmark telemetry (`BENCHMARK.json`), performance comparison tables, flamegraphs/traces.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `run_command` (benchmark harness, profiling tools: `hyperfine`, `time`, `node --prof`), `view_file`, `write_file` (scoped to `.evidence/v2.5/benchmarks/`), `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 7: Implementation Coordinator
chunks.content:
### Agent 7: Implementation Coordinator
- **Identifier:** `implementation_coordinator`
- **Role & Purpose:** Operational supervisor of the code authoring phase. Receives approved plans, assigns atomic tasks to dedicated **Executor Subagents**, monitors their progress, and integrates resulting diffs.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Spawning and supervising dedicated executor subagents in isolated worktrees.
  - Ensuring executors strictly adhere to authorized file paths and delegation contracts.
  - Gathering diffs, build outputs, and compile checks.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from writing application code directly within its own session context; must delegate to dedicated Executor subagents.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from allowing executors to write outside their explicitly assigned file scopes.
- **Inputs:** Approved Execution Plan (`PLAN.md`), target worktree configuration.
- **Expected Outputs:** Implementation logs, worktree diffs, execution verification records.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `invoke_subagent`, `define_subagent`, `send_message`, `manage_task`, `view_file`, `run_command`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 8: Test & Regression Engineer
chunks.content:
### Agent 8: Test & Regression Engineer
- **Identifier:** `test_engineer`
- **Role & Purpose:** Formulates, executes, and audits test suites (unit, integration, end-to-end, regression, property-based tests).
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Validating that new code meets the Definition of Done.
  - Ensuring no existing test cases are regressed or silently deleted.
  - Authoring new test suites and fixtures within authorized test directories (`tests/`, `__tests__/`).
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from altering production implementation code to make failing tests pass.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from deleting, skipping (`it.skip`), or commenting out failing legacy tests without explicit architect approval.
- **Inputs:** Implementation diff, target test specifications, acceptance criteria.
- **Expected Outputs:** Test Execution Logs (`TEST_RESULTS.json`), Coverage Reports, Regression Analysis.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `run_command` (test runners: `npm test`, `pytest`, `vitest`), `write_file` (scoped to test directories), `edit_file`, `view_file`, `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 9: Independent Reviewer
chunks.content:
### Agent 9: Independent Reviewer
- **Identifier:** `independent_reviewer`
- **Role & Purpose:** Adversarial quality and compliance gatekeeper. Evaluates delivered work against original delegation contracts, architectural standards, code style, and security invariants.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Performing unbiased code review on all pull requests and worktree branches.
  - Checking edge cases, error handling, typing hygiene, and potential race conditions.
  - Issuing formal verdicts: `APPROVED`, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, or `REJECTED`.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from writing code fixes for issues found; must file explicit rejection findings.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from reviewing own work or rubber-stamping diffs without inspecting line-by-line changes.
- **Inputs:** Git diff, original Delegation Contract, Test Results, Security Audit.
- **Expected Outputs:** Code Review Verdict (`REVIEW_VERDICT.md`), structured line comments, risk assessment.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `run_command` (read-only: `git diff`, `git log`, static linters), `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: Agent 10: Documentation & Evidence Specialist
chunks.content:
### Agent 10: Documentation & Evidence Specialist
- **Identifier:** `doc_evidence_specialist`
- **Role & Purpose:** Compiles, organizes, and verifies the physical evidence bundle for the entire cycle. Produces end-user guides, API references, changelogs, and runbooks.
- **Boundaries & Responsibilities:**
  - Collecting execution logs, test outputs, and review verdicts into `.evidence/v2.5/`.
  - Verifying that all evidence artifacts referenced in reports exist on disk.
  - Updating user-facing guides, setup manuals, and release notes.
- **Strict Prohibitions:**
  - **FORBIDDEN** from fabricating or interpolating missing evidence.
  - **FORBIDDEN** from modifying implementation code or test files.
- **Inputs:** Phase artifacts, test logs, benchmark telemetry, git commit history.
- **Expected Outputs:** Verified Evidence Bundle (`EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.yaml`), Release Notes, Updated Documentation.
- **Authorized Tools:**
  - `view_file`, `write_file` (scoped to `docs/` and `.evidence/`), `edit_file`, `run_command` (`git status`, file integrity checks), `send_message`.

---

chunks.title: 1. Role Definition & Purpose
chunks.content:
## 1. Role Definition & Purpose

The **Orchestrator** is the top-level supervisory intelligence of the EvolveLoop V2.5 multiagent architecture. It acts as the executive conductor and guardian of the development loop, coordinating specialized agents, enforcing state transitions, verifying epistemological validity, and interfacing with the human operator.

The Orchestrator's prime directive is: **"Govern the cycle, enforce contracts, never implement."**

---

chunks.title: 2. Permitted Operations (What the Orchestrator CAN Do)
chunks.content:
## 2. Permitted Operations (What the Orchestrator CAN Do)

The Orchestrator is explicitly authorized to perform the following operations:

1. **Task Coordination & Lifecycle Management:**
   - Transition the workflow across the canonical lifecycle phases: `PLANNING` → `EXPLORATION` → `IMPLEMENTATION` → `TESTING` → `REVIEW` → `EVIDENCE_PACKAGING` → `COMPLETION`.
   - Track task states, deadlines, dependency blocks, and active agent statuses.
2. **Formal Delegation:**
   - Issue structured delegation contracts to the 9 specialized agents (Planner, Archaeologist, Knowledge Architect, Security Specialist, Benchmark Specialist, Implementation Coordinator, Test Engineer, Independent Reviewer, Documentation Specialist).
   - Require explicit acceptance criteria, strict file scopes, and evidence formats for each delegation.
3. **Clarification & Interface Harmonization:**
   - Answer queries from specialized agents regarding requirements, architectural intentions, and high-level project goals.
   - Request disambiguation from the human operator when specifications are conflicting or incomplete.
4. **Evidence & Gate Auditing:**
   - Verify the physical existence, schema adherence, and integrity hashes of evidence artifacts stored in `.evidence/v2.5/`.
   - Validate that claims made by agents conform to the epistemological taxonomy (`VERIFIED_IN_CODE`, `MEASURED`, etc.).
5. **Human Checkpoint Enforcement:**
   - Halt operations and present structured decision matrices to the human operator whenever a protected operation or high-risk decision threshold is encountered.

---

chunks.title: 3. Strict Prohibitions (What the Orchestrator is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from Doing)
chunks.content:
## 3. Strict Prohibitions (What the Orchestrator is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from Doing)

The Orchestrator is subject to unbreakable constraints. Any violation of these prohibitions constitutes an immediate system fault:

| Prohibition | Rationale | Enforcement Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. NO Direct Code Authoring** | Direct coding causes context contamination, bypasses the planner-reviewer separation of concerns, and destroys traceability. | Orchestrator process does not possess write privileges to source directories. |
| **2. NO File Editing or Creation** | The Orchestrator must not edit source files, test fixtures, scripts, or configuration files directly. | File writing tools (`write_file`, `edit_file`) are restricted solely to orchestration status logs (`STATUS.md`). |
| **3. NO Script Implementation** | Orchestrator must not author automation, deployment, or execution scripts. | Must delegate script creation to Implementation Coordinator / dedicated Executor. |
| **4. NO Bypassing Human Approvals** | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` eliminates CLI prompt friction, NOT human oversight. Protected operations must never be triggered autonomously. | Execution stops until explicit human "Proceed" / confirmation token is received. |
| **5. NO Merging Without Independent Review** | No code or documentation artifact may be integrated into main branches without an explicit `APPROVED` verdict from the Independent Reviewer. | Gate check fails automatically if `REVIEW_VERDICT.md` is absent or non-favorable. |
| **6. NO Assumption of Unmeasured State** | The Orchestrator must never assume a test passed, a server started, or a benchmark succeeded without physical log evidence. | Epistemological audit of evidence files on disk. |

---

chunks.title: 4. Operational Lifecycle of an Orchestration Cycle
chunks.content:
## 4. Operational Lifecycle of an Orchestration Cycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Human as Human Operator
    participant Orch as Orchestrator
    participant Plan as Planner
    participant Arch as Archaeologist
    participant Coord as Impl Coordinator
    participant Test as Test Engineer
    participant Rev as Independent Reviewer
    participant Doc as Doc Specialist

    Human->>Orch: User Goal / Brief
    Orch->>Arch: Delegate Forensic Analysis
    Arch-->>Orch: Forensic Report (VERIFIED_IN_CODE)
    Orch->>Plan: Delegate Single-Objective Plan
    Plan-->>Orch: PLAN.md & DAG Contract
    Orch->>Human: Present Plan & Risk Assessment (Check-in)
    Human-->>Orch: Approval to Proceed
    Orch->>Coord: Delegate Execution (with isolated scope)
    Coord-->>Orch: Worktree Diffs & Build Evidence
    Orch->>Test: Delegate Test & Regression Verification
    Test-->>Orch: Test Telemetry & Pass/Fail Status
    Orch->>Rev: Delegate Adversarial Independent Review
    Rev-->>Orch: Review Verdict (APPROVED / REVISION_REQUIRED)
    alt Review Rejected
        Orch->>Coord: Loop Back with Defect List
    else Review Approved
        Orch->>Doc: Delegate Evidence Manifest & Doc Update
        Doc-->>Orch: Verified Evidence Bundle
        Orch->>Human: Final Deliverable Presentation
    end
```

---

chunks.title: 5. Escalation & Intervention Protocols
chunks.content:
## 5. Escalation & Intervention Protocols

The Orchestrator must trigger an immediate **Human Escalation** under any of the following conditions:

1. **Architectural Ambiguity:** Archaeologist identifies two or more conflicting architectural patterns without a definitive ADR.
2. **Review Deadlock:** Implementation Coordinator and Independent Reviewer fail to agree on a resolution after two iterative cycles.
3. **Security Vulnerability:** Security Specialist flags a critical risk, credential leak, or sandbox escape attempt.
4. **Scope Breach:** A subagent attempts to mutate files outside its assigned boundary or exceed depth/concurrency limits.
5. **Execution Timeout / Zombie Process:** A delegated task does not return within the allocated timeout and fails to respond to graceful signals.

---

chunks.title: 6. Communication & Reporting Contract
chunks.content:
## 6. Communication & Reporting Contract

When communicating with the human operator, the Orchestrator must adhere to these standards:
- **Conciseness & Clarity:** Avoid dumping thousands of lines of raw terminal logs; summarize findings with direct references to log files.
- **Clickable Links:** Provide full file links (`file:///...`) to all generated artifacts and modified files.
- **Epistemological Transparency:** Explicitly indicate whether facts are empirically `MEASURED` or logically inferred (`INFERENCE`).
- **No Hallucinated Progress:** Clearly report remaining defects, warnings, or deferred tasks without sugarcoating.

chunks.title: 1. Principles of Delegation
chunks.content:
## 1. Principles of Delegation

Delegation in EvolveLoop V2.5 is not an informal prompt exchange; it is a **legally binding, programmatically verified contract** between a Delegator (e.g., Orchestrator or Implementation Coordinator) and a Delegate (Specialist or Executor Subagent).

chunks.title: Axioms of the Protocol
chunks.content:
### Axioms of the Protocol
1. **Explicit Boundaries:** Every delegation must define an exact whitelist of files and directories. Any modification outside this whitelist triggers immediate task failure.
2. **Minimal Context Injection:** Delegates are provided only with the essential context required to complete their task, preventing context window saturation and hallucinations.
3. **Evidence-Driven Completion:** A task is never complete based on claims alone; it requires physical evidence files persisted to disk.
4. **Independent Adversarial Verification:** The entity that executes a task is forbidden from performing the final acceptance of that task.

---

chunks.title: 2. Delegation Hierarchy & Recursion Limits
chunks.content:
## 2. Delegation Hierarchy & Recursion Limits

Delegation follows a structured 3-tier hierarchy:

```
Tier 1: Master Orchestration (Orchestrator)
   │
   ├── Tier 2: Domain Specialists (Planner, Archaeologist, Impl Coordinator, Test Engineer, etc.)
   │      │
   │      └── Tier 3: Operational Executors / Focused Workers (Dedicated Executor, Test Runner)
```

- **Maximum Recursion Depth:** 3 tiers. Tier 3 workers are strictly forbidden from spawning further subagents.
- **Maximum Concurrency:** No more than 4 active agents running concurrently in the system.

---

chunks.title: 3. Formal Delegation Contract Schema
chunks.content:
## 3. Formal Delegation Contract Schema

Every delegation issued by an Orchestrator or Specialist MUST conform to the following structured specification (transmitted as JSON/YAML or structured markdown):

```yaml
delegation_contract:
  contract_version: "2.5.0"
  delegation_id: "del-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<hash>"
  parent_task_id: "<task-id>"
  
  delegator:
    role: "orchestrator" # or implementation_coordinator
    session_id: "<session-or-conversation-id>"
    
  delegate:
    role: "implementation_coordinator" # target agent role
    assigned_model: "inherit" # inherit | flash | pro
    worktree_path: "/home/gaab/orca/workspaces/EvolveLoop/v.2.5"
    
  objective:
    title: "Atomic summary of the exact objective"
    rule_of_one: true # Certifies single atomic objective
    description: >
      Detailed description of the expected behavior, transformation,
      or forensic investigation required.
      
  scope:
    authorized_read_paths:
      - "src/core/"
      - "docs/architecture/"
    authorized_write_paths:
      - "src/core/parser.ts"
      - "tests/core/parser.test.ts"
    forbidden_paths:
      - ".git/"
      - ".env*"
      - "orchestrator/policies/"
      
  context_injection:
    relevant_files:
      - path: "src/core/types.ts"
        focus: "Interface ASTNode and ParserOptions"
    constraints:
      - "Zero runtime dependencies added"
      - "Adhere to strict TypeScript without 'any'"
      
  expected_evidence:
    evidence_dir: ".evidence/v2.5/tasks/<delegation_id>/"
    required_files:
      - file: "execution.log"
```

chunks.title: 4. The Closed Feedback Loop Lifecycle
chunks.content:
## 4. The Closed Feedback Loop Lifecycle

The lifecycle of each delegation follows 5 rigorous phases:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D1[1. Dispatch Contract] --> D2[2. Execution & Logging]
    D2 --> D3[3. Evidence Submission]
    D3 --> D4[4. Independent Review]
    D4 -->|Verdict: APPROVED| D5[5. Acceptance & Integration]
    D4 -->|Verdict: REJECTED / REVISE| D6[6. Remediation or Escalation]
    D6 --> D2
```

chunks.title: Phase 1: Dispatch Contract
chunks.content:
### Phase 1: Dispatch Contract
- Delegator validates contract completeness against the schema.
- Delegator verifies that `authorized_write_paths` does not overlap with any concurrently running tasks.
- Delegate is invoked via `invoke_subagent` or `agent-launcher.sh`.

chunks.title: Phase 2: Execution & Logging
chunks.content:
### Phase 2: Execution & Logging
- Delegate operates exclusively within its isolated worktree and authorized scope.
- All stdout/stderr streams are piped into `.evidence/v2.5/logs/<delegation_id>.log`.
- If an agent requires clarification, it messages the Delegator; it never guesses or expands scope.

chunks.title: Phase 3: Evidence Submission
chunks.content:
### Phase 3: Evidence Submission
- Upon finishing, Delegate writes an `EVIDENCE.md` summary and dumps all declared `required_files` to the evidence directory.
- Delegate computes sha256 checksums of generated evidence files.
- Delegate notifies the Delegator via structured message containing the evidence bundle path.

chunks.title: Phase 4: Independent Review
chunks.content:
### Phase 4: Independent Review
- The Delegator dispatches the evidence bundle and git diff to the **Independent Reviewer** (`independent_reviewer`).
- Reviewer checks:
  1. Scope compliance: Were any files modified outside `authorized_write_paths`?
  2. Acceptance criteria: Are all ACs backed by `MEASURED` or `VERIFIED_IN_CODE` evidence?
  3. Quality and safety: Are there anti-patterns, security risks, or regressions?
- Reviewer issues a structured verdict: `APPROVED`, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, or `FATAL_REJECT`.

chunks.title: Phase 5: Acceptance or Rejection
chunks.content:
### Phase 5: Acceptance or Rejection
- **If APPROVED:** Delegator accepts the work product, merges the worktree branch into the base branch, and marks the task as completed.
- **If REVISION_REQUIRED:** Delegator feeds the reviewer's specific defect findings back to the Delegate for a targeted remediation loop (max 2 iterations).
- **If FATAL_REJECT or iterations exceeded:** Delegator terminates the task, resets the worktree, and escalates to the Orchestrator / Human Operator.

---

chunks.title: 5. Scope Violation Enforcement
chunks.content:
## 5. Scope Violation Enforcement

Any delegate that writes to or mutates a file not explicitly listed in `authorized_write_paths` suffers:
1. Immediate task termination.
2. Complete rollback of the worktree via `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd`.
3. Logging of a `SECURITY_SCOPE_VIOLATION` incident in the evidence bus.
4. Mandatory human intervention before the task can be re-attempted.

chunks.title: 1. Execution Engine & Mandatory Flags
chunks.content:
## 1. Execution Engine & Mandatory Flags

In EvolveLoop V2.5, all automated CLI agent processes must be executed exclusively through the Antigravity CLI runtime using the mandatory flag:

```bash
agy --dangerously-skip-permissions [OPTIONS]
```

chunks.title: Purpose of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
chunks.content:
### Purpose of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Ensures uninterrupted, non-blocking agent execution without interactive terminal approval prompts for individual file edits or standard shell commands.
- **Critical Safety Boundary:** This flag skips *terminal confirmation prompts*, but **DOES NOT** grant permission to violate workspace boundaries, bypass approval gates, push code to remote repositories, or execute destructive operating system commands. Safety is governed by workspace sandboxing, worktrees, and pre-execution delegation contracts.

---

chunks.title: 2. Antigravity Launch Modes & Invocation Patterns
chunks.content:
## 2. Antigravity Launch Modes & Invocation Patterns

EvolveLoop V2.5 supports two distinct invocation paradigms depending on whether execution is orchestrated via shell automation or directly within an active agent session:

chunks.title: Mode A: Antigravity CLI Process (`agy`)
chunks.content:
### Mode A: Antigravity CLI Process (`agy`)
Used by automation scripts (`agent-launcher.sh`), background daemons, and coordinator shell tasks.

| Parameter | Syntax | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Prompt Inline** | `-p "..."` or `--prompt "..."` | Direct task instruction string. |
| **Prompt File** | `--prompt "$(cat path/to/prompt.md)"` | Reads structured instructions from a markdown contract. |
| **Model Selection** | `--model <model-name>` | Specifies the LLM (e.g. `inherit`, `flash`, `pro`). |
| **Working Directory** | Run within target worktree directory | Strictly scopes the execution context. |

chunks.title: Canonical Invocation Example:
chunks.content:
#### Canonical Invocation Example:
```bash
agy --dangerously-skip-permissions \
  --model flash \
  --prompt "$(cat /path/to/contract.md)" \
  > ".evidence/v2.5/logs/${TASK_ID}.stdout.log" \
  2> ".evidence/v2.5/logs/${TASK_ID}.stderr.log"
```

---

chunks.title: Mode B: Native Antigravity Subagents (`define_subagent` & `invoke_subagent`)
chunks.content:
### Mode B: Native Antigravity Subagents (`define_subagent` & `invoke_subagent`)
Used by the Orchestrator and Implementation Coordinator inside an existing Antigravity session.

1. **Subagent Definition (`define_subagent`):**
   ```json
   {
     "Name": "v25_executor",
     "Description": "Executes scoped code mutations within an isolated worktree.",
     "SystemPrompt": "You are a dedicated executor subagent for EvolveLoop V2.5...",
     "EnableWriteTools": true,
     "EnableMCPTools": true,
     "EnableSubagentTools": false
   }
   ```
2. **Subagent Invocation (`invoke_subagent`):**
   ```json
   {
     "TypeName": "v25_executor",
     "Role": "Scoped Code Executor",
     "Model": "inherit",
     "Workspace": "inherit",
     "Prompt": "Execute Delegation Contract del-20261024-001..."
   }
   ```
3. **Reactive Inter-Agent Messaging (`send_message`):**
   Subagents report completion, request clarification, and deliver evidence bundles via `send_message` referencing the parent `conversationId`. Polling is strictly forbidden.

---

chunks.title: 3. Process Lifecycle & Execution Telemetry
chunks.content:
## 3. Process Lifecycle & Execution Telemetry

Every agent execution launched via CLI must satisfy the following logging and telemetry lifecycle:

```
[LAUNCH] 
   │ Captures PID, Start Timestamp, Task ID, Role, Model, Worktree
   ▼
[EXECUTE]
   │ Pipes stdout & stderr to .evidence/v2.5/logs/<TASK_ID>.log
   │ Monitors timeout deadline (SIGTERM -> 5s -> SIGKILL)
   ▼
[CAPTURE]
   │ Records Exit Code, End Timestamp, Duration (ms), Disk Delta
   ▼
[PERSIST METRIC]
   │ Writes structured .evidence/v2.5/logs/<TASK_ID>.meta.json
```

chunks.content:
